To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) ageing differently affects the adrenal functions; (2) the loss of T rhythmicity in elderly men is confirmed, but a significant fT rhythm is recorded; (3) this finding leads us to consider fT more sensitive than total testosterone in studying circadian rhythms of gonadal secretion.

ageing differently affects glucocorticoid (cortisol) and androgen (dehydroepiandrosteone sulphate) secretion, and that free testosterone (f T) circadian rhythm is not related to sex hormone-binding globulins (SHBG) modifications in elderly men.

ageing differentially affects the two major functions of the adrenal cortex, glucocorticoids and androgens, and that the circadian rhythms of free testosterone, but not of total testosterone, can be used to study gonadal androgen secretions in elderly men.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the circadian rhythms of adrenal androgens and their relationship with other hormones.
the study of the circadian rhythms of the main androgens, and their metabolites in the serum of normal men, in order to understand the mechanisms of age-related changes in male androgen secretion.
the circadian rhythms of plasma DHA-s, T and fT in elderly men.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the circadian rhythm of DHA-s secretion is selectively lost in elderly males, whereas fT is still able to reflect a circadian rhythm of the testicular androgen production in elderly men.
ageing is characterized by a selective impairment of the adrenal function and by the preservation of the gonadal function, at least as far as the circadian rhythm is concerned.
ageing affects differently the two major adrenal secretions, glucocorticoids and androgens, and that the loss of T rhythm is not a simple reflection of the loss of adrenal androgen secretion.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the circadian rhythms of T and DHA-s, which are both under the influence of the hypothalamo-pituitary-adrenocortical axis, are differently affected by ageing.
in elderly subjects the loss of T rhythmicity is associated with a selective impairment of the adrenal androgen function.
the circadian rhythm of adrenal androgen secretion, which is lost during ageing, may be related to the loss of circadian rhythm of T in the elderly men.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the circadian rhythms of DHA-S and fT are altered in elderly men, whereas the circadian rhythms for SHBG, cortisol, T, LH, FSH and oestradiol are maintained.
the circadian rhythms of testosterone, free testosterone, cortisol, and DHA-s are altered in older men.

the circadian rhythms of testosterone and free testosterone are affected by ageing, and that the free testosterone rhythm is more sensitive and more reliable in detecting the changes in the circadian rhythm of the androgen secretion.
